DecoupleR integration

2024-02-27

spacedeconv_decoupleR.Rmd

We provide wrapper functions to spatially quantify Pathway and Transcription Factor activities using DecoupleR.

library(spacedeconv)
## → Setting up spacedeconv environment..
## → Using conda environment 'spacedeconv-env'
library(decoupleR)

Built-in references can be retrieved via decoupleR by selecting the reference database with the method argument: “progeny”, “dorothea”, or “collectri”. Custom reference tables can also be supplied directly, as shown below.

ref <- get_decoupleR_reference(method = "progeny", organism = "human")
## ── spacedeconv ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
## ℹ Getting decoupleR reference
## ✔ Got decoupleR reference [5s]
## 
head(ref)
## # A tibble: 6 × 4
##   source   target  weight  p_value
##   <chr>    <chr>    <dbl>    <dbl>
## 1 Androgen TMPRSS2  11.5  2.38e-47
## 2 Androgen NKX3-1   10.6  2.21e-44
## 3 Androgen MBOAT2   10.5  4.63e-44
## 4 Androgen KLK2     10.2  1.94e-40
## 5 Androgen SARG     11.4  2.79e-40
## 6 Androgen SLC38A4   7.36 1.25e-39

In the next step the activities can be computed.

data("spatial_data_3")
spatial_data_3 <- preprocess(spatial_data_3)
## ── spacedeconv ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
## ℹ testing parameter
## ✔ parameter OK [51ms]
## 
## ℹ Removing 137 observations with umi count below threshold
## ✔ Removed 137 observations with umi count below threshold [937ms]
## 
## ℹ Removing 13049 variables with all zero expression
## Warning in preprocess(spatial_data_3): There are 13 mitochondrial genes
## present. Consider removing them.
## ✔ Removed 13049 variables with all zero expression [177ms]
## 
## ℹ Checking for ENSEMBL Identifiers
## ! Warning: ENSEMBL identifiers detected in gene names
## ℹ Checking for ENSEMBL Identifiersℹ Consider using Gene Names for first-generation deconvolution tools
## ℹ Checking for ENSEMBL Identifiers✔ Finished Preprocessing [9ms]
spatial_data_3 <- spacedeconv::normalize(spatial_data_3)
## ── spacedeconv ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
## ℹ testing parameter
## ✔ parameter OK [15ms]
## 
## ℹ Normalizing using cpm
## ✔ Finished normalization using cpm [2.8s]
## 
## ℹ Please note the normalization is stored in an additional assay

spe <- compute_activities(spatial_data_3, reference = ref, method = "wmean", assay = "cpm")
## ── spacedeconv ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
## ℹ testing parameter
## ✔ parameter OK [11ms]
## 
## ℹ Running decoupleR
## → Calculated multiple results, using corr_wmean  , other available results:  norm_wmeanCalculated multiple results, using corr_wmean  , other available results:  wmean
## ℹ Running decoupleR✔ Finished [27.5s]

Custom references can be passed directly to compute_activities() as a table with source (gene set or regulator), target (gene identifier), and weight. Use weight 1 for unsigned membership, or biologically justified weights when available. Gene identifiers must match the expression assay row names and organism. At least five matching genes per set are required, and each source-target pair should occur only once. Activity scoring methods such as ULM use the supplied weights, whereas AUCell, FGSEA, GSVA, and ORA ignore them.

# Illustrative genes only; use a validated signature or database gene set for analysis.
ref <- data.frame(
  source = rep("my_signature", 5),
  target = c("STAT1", "IRF1", "CXCL9", "CXCL10", "IDO1"),
  weight = rep(1, 5)
)
spe <- compute_activities(spatial_data_3, reference = ref, method = "ulm", assay = "cpm")
# Scores are stored in colData(spe), e.g. spe$decoupleR_my_signature.

For example, MSigDB Hallmark gene sets can be retrieved via decoupleR and converted to a custom reference. This example uses human gene symbols. The initial download retrieves the full MSigDB resource and may take a while.

msigdb <- decoupleR::get_resource("MSigDB")
hallmark <- subset(msigdb, collection == "hallmark")
ref <- unique(data.frame(source = hallmark$geneset, target = hallmark$genesymbol))
ref <- ref[!is.na(ref$target) & nzchar(ref$target), ]
ref$weight <- 1

# Optional: keep only selected Hallmark gene sets.
# ref <- ref[ref$source %in% c("HALLMARK_HYPOXIA", "HALLMARK_INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE"), ]

spe <- compute_activities(spatial_data_3, reference = ref, method = "ulm", assay = "cpm")
# Example result columns:
# spe$decoupleR_HALLMARK_HYPOXIA
# spe$decoupleR_HALLMARK_INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE
